# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** Housemother  <sub>[v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunty  <sub>[v3 c35 P2](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0002), [v3 c35 P22](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0022)</sub>; Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c19 P41](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0041), [v3 c36 P0](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Jamesina is a tiny old woman with a softly-triangular face and pink cheeks. She has snow-white hair worn in quaint little puffs over her ears, and large, soft blue eyes filled with youth and hope.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina describes herself as old-fashioned in her opinions and clothing, preferring comfort over modern trends. She possesses young, twinkling eyes and a mirthful disposition, maintaining an open-minded attitude about letting young people manage their own behavior. She candidly acknowledges her past flaws, such as laughing at her former suitors or holding grudges, but believes carrying spite is not worth while with age.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c18 P2](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0002), [v3 c35 P15](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0015), [v3 c35 P17](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0017), [v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)_

## Traits

- Old-fashioned  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>
- Good-natured and tolerant  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>
- Candid and honest  <sub>[v3 c35 P15](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0015)</sub>

## Abilities

- Knitting  <sub>[v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>

## Goals

- Keep house for the college girls at Patty's Place  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c18 P1](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0001)</sub>

## History

Aunt Jamesina agreed to join Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Philippa Gordon, and Stella at Patty's Place to act as their housemother while they attended Redmond College. She arrived bringing two cats: the Sarah-cat, given to her by her washerwoman, and Joseph, a multi-colored cat entrusted to her by a friend who moved to Vancouver. During the Christmas holidays, she chose to stay behind at Patty's Place to care for the cats rather than leave them alone. At Patty's Place, she kept house, knitted by the fire, listened to the girls' stories, shared anecdotes of her youthful suitors, and offered her pragmatic perspective on writing and romance.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P5](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0005), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P55](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0055), [v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058), [v3 c16 P59](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0059), [v3 c18 P0](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0000), [v3 c18 P1](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0001), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005), [v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021), [v3 c35 P25](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0025), [v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)_

## Background by volume

- Had numerous suitors in her youth, including Jim Elwood, Dan Winston, Milton Edwards, and Horatio Reeve  <sub>[v3 c35 P25](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0025)</sub>
- Her daughter wrote stories before becoming a foreign missionary  <sub>[v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)</sub>
- Her husband used to refer to her washerwoman's cat as the Sarah-cat  <sub>[v3 c16 P59](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0059)</sub>

## Quotes

> New shoes are smarter than old ones, but the old ones are more comfortable. I’m old enough to indulge myself in the matter of shoes and opinions.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> You’re old enough to know how to behave if you’re ever going to be. So, as far as I am concerned, you can all go to destruction in your own way.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> There are three old widowers at home who have been casting sheep’s eyes at me for some time. You children needn’t think you own all the romance in the world.  <sub>[v3 c35 P23](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0023)</sub>

> I’ve a notion that such prayers don’t rise very far. I used to pray that I might be enabled to forgive a certain person, but I know now I really didn’t want to forgive her.  <sub>[v3 c35 P15](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0015)</sub>

> It isn’t in good taste to make fun of your beaux, but I always did it myself.  <sub>[v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)</sub>
